Subject: Budget range validation - Avalon Finance

Hi Sam —

Great talking earlier today — thanks for walking us through Avalon’s pilot use cases (transactional summaries + customer support routing). To keep momentum, wanted to confirm a few budget/pricing points so we can put together an accurate committed-tier proposal and SOW: 

Recap of ask/need:
- Primary workloads: short-form generative responses (average 200 tokens/generation) + embeddings for search/rerank.
- Expected monthly token volume range (your estimate): ?
- Target unit economics / target $ per 1M tokens you’re comfortable with: ?
- Procurement thresholds: PO size that triggers legal review or multi-week procurement cycles?

What we’ll deliver after we confirm numbers: Redwood committed-tier deck (pricing by monthly token band), a draft SOW, and a 30-day pilot quote that maps to your procurement timeline. I attached a short pricing summary with our standard committed tiers to give you a baseline.

Quick questions to help us size things properly:
1) Can you confirm the expected monthly tokens (low / mid / high scenario)?
2) For unit economics, is there a target $/1M tokens you need us to hit for the business case?
3) What procurement/PO thresholds and timeline should we plan for?

Next steps: if you can reply with those three items, I’ll have a tailored committed-tier proposal over to you by EOD Friday.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@avalonfinance.com>

Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - Avalon Finance

Hey Marissa —

Thanks for the follow-up and the pricing sheet — helpful. Quick answers below based on our internal forecasting (still somewhat rough):

1) Monthly token volume (low / mid / high):
- Low: ~20M tokens/month (pilot, limited customers)
- Mid: ~60M tokens/month (first 6 months post-pilot)
- High: ~150M tokens/month (broader rollout into Customer Support)

2) Target unit economics: our FP&A team is modeling around $60–$80 per 1M tokens as the threshold for the project to be ROI-positive (this accounts for downstream infra/costs). If you can get committed pricing in that band for mid/high usage, that would look good internally.

3) Procurement thresholds & timeline:
- Purchases under $25k can be approved by procurement in ~5 business days.
- Anything over $25k requires legal review and a contract (additional 2–3 weeks typical).
- For pilot budgets (which will be < $25k), procurement can do a short PO. For committed contracts we’ll need SOW + Master Agreement.

I attached our forecasting workbook so you can map pricing to their scenarios. Happy to jump on a quick 20-min follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Sam
Director, Product Ops | Avalon Finance
sam.patel@avalonfinance.com

Attachments: Avalon-forecast.pdf (monthly token scenarios)

Sam — thanks for the fast reply and the numbers, that’s exactly what we needed. Couple of clarifying Qs from the pricing/solutions side so we can size committed tiers properly: 

- Token mix: are the 200-token/generation numbers for generation-only, and do embeddings consumption sit separately? We typically price embeddings differently since the unit cost per token for embedding workloads and QPS/latency expectations differ.
- Do you expect a steady-state distribution (e.g., 70% generation / 30% embeddings) or will it shift over time?

Based on the 60M mid-case and your $60–$80 target per 1M tokens, we can put together:
1) A pilot PO-friendly quote (~20M tokens, price per 1M at list + pilot discount) that stays under $25k so procurement can sign off quickly.
2) Committed-tier options for 50–100M and 100–200M bands with stepped discounts tied to committed monthly volumes; we’ll show effective $/1M tokens for each band so it’s easy to compare to your $60–$80 target.

If you confirm the token mix (generation vs embeddings) I’ll include both unitized pricing and an example invoice run-rate for the mid/high scenarios.

Thanks —
Dylan
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Hi Marissa / Sam —

Confirming procurement policy items per Sam’s note:
- PO approvals under $25,000: procurement can approve with standard vendor onboarding (5 business days).
- Purchases >= $25,000: require Legal + Master Services Agreement (we typically allow 2–3 weeks for review).

Required items to issue a pilot PO: W-9, invoice remit address, and a brief statement of work (1 page) describing the deliverable and pilot duration. For any committed spend we will need a signed Master Agreement and SOW.

You can send onboarding docs to procurement@avalonfinance.com. We prefer invoices/attachments as PDFs.
